text: dsh-api-thinking（DSH 插件，任意客户端）：自动读取第三方 API 路由公布的模型思考档位，并同步到 DSH 的模型配置。它挂接 llm-pi-ai profile，通过模型清单识别支持的 reasoningEfforts，再经配置编辑器更新对应模型。支持 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 风格的模型清单、定时及配置变更后扫描、可选显示 off 或固定档位，并记录扫描状态。适合使用第三方模型路由并希望模型选择器反映实际推理档位的用户。需要配置相应模型路由；插件按路由配置请求其模型清单。

dsh-api-thinking (DSH plugin) syncs reasoning levels from third-party listings to llm-pi-ai. It scans at startup, periodically, or after profile changes; supports fixed and optional off levels; and records status. Useful when model pickers should reflect endpoint capabilities.
想让 DSH 自动显示第三方模型支持的思考强度。
新增模型路由后，能不能自动同步它的推理档位？
不想每次手动维护模型的 reasoningEfforts 配置。
让模型选择器按 API 实际公布的能力显示思考选项。
DSH 里第三方模型没有思考档位，怎么根据模型清单补齐？
希望模型配置变化后自动重新读取各路由的模型列表。
Keep DSH reasoning levels in sync with what each model endpoint publishes.
Can new third-party routes get their thinking options updated automatically?
I want the model picker to show the reasoning levels supported by my API gateway.
How can I avoid manually maintaining per-model thinking settings?
模型思考档位同步：读取兼容路由返回的模型清单，将模型公布的可用档位映射到 reasoningEfforts，并更新 llm-pi-ai 配置。扫描由启动延迟、周期定时或 profile 变更触发。
固定档位与关闭选项：端点未给出档位集合但公布固定 effort 时，可将它作为唯一档位；端点允许关闭时也可配置是否加入 off。
状态诊断：加载和每次扫描会合并写入状态文档，记录阶段、路由结果、变更通道和错误；可指定文件路径或关闭状态写入。
配置文件回退更新：配置编辑器写入遇到嵌套 HMR 事务时，插件可直接规划并写入 profile patch，同时以临时文件替换目标文件。
dsh-api-thinking 使用每条模型路由配置的 baseURL 请求模型清单；若路由配置了凭据，也会随请求发送认证信息。
dsh-api-thinking README · Introduction：<div align="center">

dsh-api-thinking README · api_thinking：**Reads each third-party API's own model listing and syncs every model's real thinking levels into DSH** [中文](README.zh.md) · [MIT](LICENSE) [](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-api-thinking) [](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-api-thinking) [](LICENSE) [](https://github.com/shuang-ying/dsh-ThirdApi-ThinkingMode/actions/workflows/test.yml) > api_thinking is a community-maintained DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin. It is not a DeepSeek AI product.

dsh-api-thinking README · The problem it solves：DSH's built-in model catalogue does not contain your third-party APIs. To get them into the model picker at all, you declare an `llm-pi-ai` route by hand and list its `models:` yourself.

But **a hand-written `models:` list replaces the installed catalogue outright**. Those models are neither in the catalogue nor declare `reasoningEfforts`, so `dsh-llm-pi-ai` treats them as non-reasoning and **the composer offers no thinking levels**.

dsh-api-thinking README · The problem it solves：Writing the levels into YAML fixes that once — and goes stale immediately: nobody adds them when the gateway ships a new model, and nobody updates them when upstream changes what it supports.

Yet an OpenAI-compatible gateway **usually already publishes that capability in its own model listing**. This plugin reads it and writes the result back into your configuration, so you stop maintaining that YAML by hand.

dsh-api-thinking README · Features：- **Automatic level sync** — requests each route's model listing and writes the levels the endpoint publishes into the matching model's `reasoningEfforts`.
- **New APIs just work** — add a route, or add models to an existing one; no plugin change, no restart.
- **Never invents capability** — an endpoint that says nothing about reasoning is left exactly as it is; hand-written levels are never erased.
- **Owns exactly one field** — it owns `reasoningEfforts` and nothing else; comments, `!!js` expressions and every other field stay as they were.
- **Idempotent** — a sweep that finds nothing to change writes no file at all.
- **Self-diagnosing** — every load and every sweep records a status document, so there is always something to read when it misbehaves.
dsh-api-thinking README · Screenshots：*Once installed, the model picker offers the thinking levels a model actually supports.*
dsh-api-thinking README · Install：Requires a working DeepSeek Harness installation. The examples use the `desktop` profile — substitute your own profile name.

dsh-api-thinking README · From the plugin page：Open **Settings → Plugins** in the DSH web UI, search for `dsh-api-thinking` and install it. An agent can also call the plugin manager's `install_bundle` directly.

dsh-api-thinking README · From the command line：```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-api-thinking
```

Restart DSH and refresh the page afterwards.

dsh-api-thinking README · Let an agent do it：Paste this to an agent that can run terminal commands and is connected to your DSH:

```text
Install dsh-api-thinking into my DSH profile, confirm it is active, and tell me how to reload.
```

dsh-api-thinking README · Uninstall：Switch it off or uninstall it from the plugin page, or remove the `dsh-api-thinking` dependency from that profile's `package.json` and delete it from the `dsh.profile.bundles` array.
dsh-api-thinking README · Usage：It works as soon as it is installed — **there is no switch to turn on**. The plugin walks every route under the `llm-pi-ai` row:

dsh-api-thinking README · Usage：| What you want | How |
| --- | --- |
| Get thinking levels on a model | Configure the route and its models in **Settings → Models** and give it a moment |
| Add a new API | Add it in the model page; the levels follow on their own |
| Narrow the scope | Set `routes` to the route names you care about; the default covers every OpenAI-compatible route |
| Change the sweep cadence | Set `intervalMs`; `0` means "sweep once after load, then stop" |
| Find out why nothing happened | Read the status document — see [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting-why-nothing-happened) |

dsh-api-thinking README · Rules：A model's capability comes from the **first matching field** in the endpoint's model listing:

| Purpose | Fields, in priority order |
| --- | --- |
| Selectable levels | `reasoning_supported_efforts` → `supported_efforts` → `reasoning_efforts` |
| Whether thinking can be turned off | `can_disable_thinking` → `reasoning_can_disable` |
| Whether it reasons at all | `supports_reasoning` → `reasoning` |
| A pinned effort | `reasoning_effort` → `fixed_effort` → `effort` |

What gets written:

dsh-api-thinking README · Rules：| The endpoint says | Written `reasoningEfforts` |
| --- | --- |
| A selectable set | `{ low: low, high: high, ... }`, filtered to the levels DSH can name (`off` / `minimal` / `low` / `medium` / `high` / `xhigh` / `max`), in escalation order |
| No set, but one pinned effort | That single level — the picker shows what the model actually runs at (selecting it is a no-op). Turn off with `fixedEffortAsLevel: false` |
| Explicit `supports_reasoning: false` | `false` |
| It reasons, but publishes neither a set nor a pinned effort | **The key is removed** (writing `false` would claim it does not reason) |
| **Nothing at all about reasoning** | **Left untouched** |
| **The model is not in the listing** | **Left untouched** |

dsh-api-thinking README · Rules：The last two are deliberate safety design: LiteLLM, vLLM and most self-hosted gateways publish no capability data, and treating that silence as "no levels" would erase hand-written configuration. **The plugin only ever acts on what the endpoint actually states.**

dsh-api-thinking README · Rules：`includeOff` defaults to off. When no level is selected, the pi-ai adapter sends the mapped `off` value as the default — so adding `off` to a model that allows disabling thinking would silently turn "provider default" into "no thinking". It has to be enabled explicitly.

dsh-api-thinking README · Configuration：```yaml
- insert:
    - id: api-thinking
      name: dsh-api-thinking
      config:

dsh-api-thinking README · Configuration：| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entryId` | `llm-pi-ai` | The profile row to read and write |
| `routes` | `[]` | Route names to manage; `[]` means every OpenAI-compatible route |
| `intervalMs` | `120000` | Re-sweep interval in milliseconds; `0` sweeps once after load |
| `startDelayMs` | `3000` | Delay before the first sweep, to let the profile finish loading |
| `timeoutMs` | `15000` | Per-endpoint model-listing timeout |
| `includeOff` | `false` | Expose `off` as a selectable level (see the caveat above) |
| `fixedEffortAsLevel` | `true` | Show a pinned effort as the single level |
| `log` | `true` | Log every change and every skipped route |
| `statusFile` | `''` | Status document path; `''` means `$DSH_HOME/api-thinking.status.json`, `false` disables it |

dsh-api-thinking README · Configuration：> **Overriding the bundle row**: an override in your profile patch must repeat `name: dsh-api-thinking` word for word, or `applyEntryPatches` skips it silently.

dsh-api-thinking README · When it runs：| Trigger | When | What it covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `start` | `startDelayMs` after load (3s by default) | Full calibration on boot or reload |
| `config-change` | After the profile patch changes (via the HMR config watcher, 2s debounce) | APIs, routes and models you just added or edited |
| `interval` | Every `intervalMs` (120s by default) | Backstop for upstream model and capability changes |

dsh-api-thinking README · When it runs：Every sweep re-reads the row's `providers` from the composed profile layers rather than from the snapshot the plugin was instantiated with — which is what makes a route you just saved visible immediately.

dsh-api-thinking README · Troubleshooting: why nothing happened：The host logger is not reliably reachable from a plugin, so every load and sweep writes its result to a status document (by default `$DSH_HOME/api-thinking.status.json`):

```json
{
  "phase": "sweep", "reason": "interval", "wrote": true, "via": "patch-file", "error": null,
  "routes": [{ "route": "my-gateway", "models": 20, "listed": 51,
               "changes": [{ "id": "example-model", "to": { "low": "low", "high": "high" } }],

Read these first:

dsh-api-thinking README · Troubleshooting: why nothing happened：| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `phase` | Current stage (`apply` / `sweep`) |
| `error` | Failure reason, including request errors the UI never shows |
| `listed` | How many models the endpoint returned |
| `models` | How many the route has configured |
| `changes` | Which models this sweep planned to change |
| `wrote` / `via` | Whether it wrote, and through which channel |
dsh-api-thinking README · Troubleshooting: why nothing happened：A non-empty `listed` with an empty `changes` usually means the endpoint publishes no reasoning capability — see [Rules](#rules).

dsh-api-thinking README · Write channels：The plugin prefers the official channel and only falls back when it has to:

| Channel | When | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `config-editor` | Normal case | `ctx.configEditor.edit()` — the official path, with file locking, schema validation and Loader reconciliation |
| `patch-file` | When the above answers `HMR transactions cannot be nested` | Edits the profile patch directly; the same config watcher recomposes it |

dsh-api-thinking README · Write channels：The fallback is unrelated to how the plugin was installed: a **hot-reloaded** plugin runs its `apply()` inside the very HMR transaction that replaced it, after which every write through the official channel is refused as a nested transaction. The fallback touches only the target models' `reasoningEfforts` (located by indentation, written to a temp file and renamed), leaving comments and every other field byte-identical.

dsh-api-thinking README · Known limitations：- It reads the **model listing** as its only source of capability. An endpoint that publishes nothing about reasoning is left alone.
- Only protocols that can list models are supported: `openai-completions`, `openai-responses`, `anthropic-messages`.
- Models are matched by exact id; no aliases or fuzzy matching.
- The default meaning of `off` is constrained by the pi-ai adapter, which cannot express "selectable but not the default".
- The fallback channel does no schema validation, only structural location.
- Writing `cordis.patch.yml` at the same time as the settings page can in theory overwrite each other; the next sweep converges again (it is idempotent).

dsh-api-thinking README · Feedback and contributing：Found a bug or have a suggestion? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/shuang-ying/dsh-ThirdApi-ThinkingMode/issues) with your DSH version, the plugin version and reproduction steps.

dsh-api-thinking README · Feedback and contributing：```bash
npm test                              # 15 checks: pure logic, patch edits, composed config, real gateway catalogue
node tools/check_live.mjs             # live profile vs gateway, per model; drift should be 0
node tools/diff_gateway_profile.mjs   # "why is my new API missing": gateway vs profile, per model
```

dsh-api-thinking README · Feedback and contributing：The maintenance tools infer locations from the environment (`DSH_HOME` / `DSH_PROFILE`, or `API_THINKING_PROFILE_DIR` / `API_THINKING_PROFILE`) and read the gateway from `API_THINKING_BASE_URL` (optionally with `API_THINKING_API_KEY`) or `API_THINKING_GATEWAY_CONFIG` (a config.json holding `{ listen, api_key }`).
